discovery: Quantum simulation of Hubbard models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI Innsbruck, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Feynman proposed using one quantum system to emulate another. Ultracold atoms in optical lattices made that idea a working laboratory method. Zoller and coworkers (1998) showed that atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. Bloch and Greiner observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition in 2002, the first direct quantum simulation of a strongly correlated lattice model. Greiner's quantum gas microscope, together with Bloch's single-site imaging and control, then allowed correlated many-body states to be read out atom by atom. With these tools, experiments have resolved antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, many-body localization, and out-of-equilibrium dynamics that theory and classical computers struggle to settle. Hundreds of groups worldwide now use this approach, and it is the basis of analog quantum simulation as a field linking condensed-matter physics and quantum information science.
